notes: mainThreadMs and mainThreadMsPerSecond use TaskDuration with timeTicks: elapsed time in main-thread tasks, not thread CPU time. Script, style, and layout durations use the same elapsed-time domain.
mainThreadCpuMs uses ThreadTime (renderer main-thread CPU). rendererCpuMs uses ProcessTime (renderer-process CPU); it excludes separate browser, GPU, and backend processes.
Positive reduction means a lower candidate value. Counts such as mounted editors are observations, not optimization scores.
Frame gaps and driver DOM readiness are not INP. Linux CPU throttling is not an M2 Air simulation.
Dockview setup is outside the measured windows and is not a cold-entry result. Core and full E2E plugin workloads remain separate; the plugin archive hash must match in both arms.
Streaming duration includes the wait for final visible content. Fixed-deadline traffic and visible-session progress are retained in the raw report.

hostMonitor.scope: Shared Linux host. No owned builds or tests ran during timed windows. Window boundaries are approximated from the first deadline browser-progress wall clock minus deadline duration; this is not a synchronized CPU trace.

observations: Streaming frame-gap p95 improves in four pairs, is equal in one, and regresses from 50 to 83.4 ms in pair 5. The candidate exceeds the baseline range of 33.4 to 50 ms.
Candidate streaming long tasks are zero in pairs 0 through 3, then seven and 48 in pairs 4 and 5. Baseline counts in those late pairs are two and eight.
Final-pair candidate main-thread task time is 11.30% higher, renderer CPU is 5.96% higher, and normal-idle main CPU is 16.32% higher. Retain these regressions.
Shared-host load rose late and available memory fell. This coincides with the late regressions but does not prove their cause.

Streaming document nodes remain near 15,300 and each arm retains four document editors and 47 running animations. Candidate style time remains lower in every streaming pair. No CPU attribution profile was captured in this timing series.
regressionInvestigation.nextStep: Capture a separate attribution or confirmation run on the same core fixture; retain this complete series and do not pool profiles with timing.

conclusions: Streaming history reads and decoded bytes fall about 96.2% in all six pairs. Full-history resets fall to zero in all pairs.
Streaming renderer CPU falls 11.43% and main-thread CPU 9.35% by median paired change; each improves in five pairs and regresses in the last.
Reduced-motion idle main-thread CPU falls 80.96% in every pair. This is a separate motion mode.
Streaming main-thread task time falls 6.90%, below the 20% target. Frame smoothness is not uniformly improved.
Two visible chats, the mounted hidden chat and its draft, all six ordered streams, and actual panel counts pass in every sample. Stored history and loaded/rendered history are distinct.
No cold-entry, MacBook Air M2, field INP, battery, or leak claim follows from this Linux comparison.
